headline_marked: PM Tarique Rahman [[apologizes for load shedding]], vows energy crisis fix
headline: PM Tarique Rahman apologizes for load shedding, vows energy crisis fix
summary: The Prime Minister expressed regret over power outages and expects the gas crisis to ease within days, while criticizing the previous administration's legacy of corruption.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has apologized to the nation for the ongoing load shedding and power outages. Speaking at a prayer meeting for the late Khaleda Zia, he expressed hope that the gas crisis would be resolved within a few days, leading to an improvement in the electricity situation.

The Prime Minister criticized those who criticize the government 'intentionally,' calling their actions reckless. He noted that the interim government had stopped the installation of LNG terminals, and the current government is now working to establish a third LNG terminal, which will take time.

To address the crisis, the government has initiated discussions with China and Malaysia. Tarique Rahman challenged the opposition to provide a solution for gas and electricity within three to six months, stating that the government would adopt any viable plan they present.

He further criticized the the previous fascist government, claiming it left behind a mega-corruption legacy through mega-projects and a debt of 3 lakh crore in the power sector. He alleged that the previous regime failed to drill new gas wells, instead handing the sector over to foreigners.

Tarique Rahman emphasized that the current government, only six months into power, is working to fulfill its electoral promises. He called for an end to the 'politics of confusion' and urged for a focus on national development and accountability through democracy.
caption:
PM Tarique Rahman apologizes for load shedding and vows to resolve the energy crisis soon.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has apologized to the nation for the ongoing load shedding and power outages. Speaking at a prayer meeting for the late Khaleda Zia, he expressed hope that the gas crisis would be resolved within a few days, leading to an improvement in the electricity situation.

The Prime Minister criticized those who criticize the government 'intentionally,' calling their actions reckless. He noted that the interim government had stopped the installation of LNG terminals, and the current government is now working to establish a third LNG terminal, which will take time.

To address the crisis, the government has initiated discussions with China and Malaysia. Tarique Rahman challenged the opposition to provide a solution for gas and electricity within three to six months, stating that the government would adopt any viable plan they present.

He further criticized the the previous fascist government, claiming it left behind a mega-corruption legacy through mega-projects and a debt of 3 lakh crore in the power sector. He alleged that the previous regime failed to drill new gas wells, instead handing the sector over to foreigners.

Tarique Rahman emphasized that the current government, only six months into power, is working to fulfill its electoral promises. He called for an end to the 'politics of confusion' and urged for a focus on national development and accountability through democracy.

headline: Pallabi child murder: Convicts' appeals listed for High Court hearing
summary: The death reference and appeals of those convicted in the murder of a child named Ramisa in Pallabi have been added to the High Court's cause list.
details: The High Court has listed the death reference and appeals of the convicts in the Pallabi child murder case for hearing.
The case involves the killing of a young girl named Ramisa in the Pallabi area of Dhaka.
The legal proceedings are now moving to the High Court to review the sentences handed down by the lower court.
